messages:
jessica: FYI customer (acme-inc) just flagged a billing spike. They say they send X-Region: us-west but ~40% of requests show routed to EU dedicated pool and billed at higher tier. Can someone look?

ryan: Can you paste a repro header/curl snippet and a sample request id from the logs?

jessica: Repro is simple, customer SDK apparently appends a newline. Here's what we used to repro locally:

```python
# repro (python requests)
import requests
headers = {'X-Region': 'us-west\n'}
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', headers=headers, json={'prompt': 'hi'})
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

We see identical behavior from their traffic. Example request id: req_2026_05_02_009874.

mina: I reproduced. Edge logs show parser rejecting header token with control char. Router fallback path picks default region (nearest-pop) which for these customers is eu-1. Log snippet:

```
[edge] 2026-05-02T14:03:12.456Z req=req_2026_05_02_009874 region_hdr="us-west\n" region_parse_err="invalid_control_char:10" selected_route=eu-1
[router] 2026-05-02T14:03:12.457Z req=req_2026_05_02_009874 region_tokens=["", "us-west"] chosen=eu-1
```

ryan: Interesting — router's region parser treats control chars (\n, \r) as separators and then uses the first token if present. If header starts with or contains consecutive separators you end up with an empty first token. Our prioritization code currently picks the first non-empty token? looks like it picked index 0 before trimming. That's a bug.

sam: Short-term mitigation: edge can normalize headers by stripping control chars and trimming whitespace before routing decision. Longer term we should reject requests with control chars in region header (400) and send guidance to SDKs.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: edge-normalize-region-headers v2026.05.02-rapid (canary -> 10% -> 100%) by @ryan in 10m.

ryan: Created ticket ROUTE-3248: "normalize and validate X-Region header; avoid empty-token fallback". Assigned to eng-runtime. Also added a temporary log-level alert to detect control-char occurrences and tag affected customers for outreach.

acme-support: Thanks team. We'll notify the customer to patch their SDK (strip trailing newline) and asked them to confirm once they redeploy. Customer asked for a retro on why billing spike happened — forwarding this thread.

jessica: Action items:
- @ryan apply edge normalization patch (canary now)
- @mina add parsing unit-tests for control characters
- @sam create billing adjustment playbook for impacted customers (list attached to ROUTE-3248)

mina: I added tests that assert we never pick an empty token as the primary region and return 400 for purely invalid values.

ryan: Canary started, 10% traffic. Early metrics: control-char hit rate 0.02% of requests; routing failures down to 0.0001% after normalization.

jessica: Marking customer ticket as "in progress" and referencing ROUTE-3248. Will follow up with billing and customer once patch is in 100%. :white_check_mark:

sam: Good catch. We'll also add a short SDK note: do not include newline/CR in header values.

(thumbs-up reactions from several people)
